title: finding(i18n): `createI18n`'s `resources` merge is one level deep, so overriding one key of an existing namespace silently drops that namespace's other keys
body:
Spotted while implementing #7454 (the `calendar.allDay` spelling) — **not fixed there**, that PR's fence is `packages/plugin-calendar`. Filed unassigned.

## Measured on `origin/main` at `ac8abb0f5`

`packages/i18n/src/i18n.ts`, inside `createI18n`:

```
for (const [lang, translations] of Object.entries(builtInLocales)) {
  mergedResources[lang] = {
    translation: {
      ...translations,
      ...(resources[lang] || {}),
    },
  };
}
```

Both spreads are **one level deep**, and the pack's top-level keys are the
namespace-ish groups (`common`, `calendar`, `list`, ...), each a nested object.
So a caller who supplies a partial group does not merge into it — they
**replace** it:

```
createI18n({ defaultLanguage: 'en', resources: { en: { calendar: { today: 'Heute' } } } })
```

leaves `calendar.today` = `Heute` and every other `calendar.*` key — `month`,
`week`, `day`, `allDay`, `newEvent`, `moreEvents`, `unscheduled` — **gone from
the instance**. `t('calendar.allDay')` then returns the bare key, which reaches
the DOM as the literal text `calendar.allDay`.

## Why the existing pin does not see it

`packages/i18n/src/__tests__/i18n.test.ts:185` is named `merges custom resources
with built-in locales`, and it does assert a merge — but only for a **new**
top-level key:

```
resources: { en: { custom: { greeting: 'Hello!' } } },
...
expect(i18n.t('custom.greeting')).toBe('Hello!');
expect(i18n.t('common.save')).toBe('Save');   // a DIFFERENT group
```

Adding a group and overriding a group are the two different operations here, and
only the first is pinned. The test's name reads as though it covered both.

## How it surfaced

#7454 deletes a `t('calendar.allDay') === 'calendar.allDay'` ternary in
`CalendarView` as unreachable. It is unreachable through
`createSafeTranslation`'s provider-less arm (that arm resolves `defaults[key]`
first) and unreachable with a provider **as long as the instance carries the
key** — which the built-in packs guarantee. This shallow merge is the one
construction that removes that guarantee. It was still right to delete the
ternary: it guarded exactly one of the seven `calendar.*` labels that file
renders, so in the scenario it protected, the other six already render raw keys.
The coherent fix is here, not a per-label guard at the call sites.

## Not judged here

Whether the merge should go one level deeper, or whether a partial group
override should be **rejected** at `createI18n` rather than quietly honoured, is
a contract question — the second is the more contract-first shape (declared =
enforced) but it could break a caller relying on replacement today. There is
also a smaller, separate option: rename or split the existing test so its name
stops promising coverage it does not have. Left to triage.

Related: #7454 (where this was found and correctly fenced out) - #7567 (the
gate-blindness half of #7454).
